items.title: LEAP-Block: left bundle-branch area pacing beats RV pacing on death, HF events or BiV upgrade in AV block with preserved EF (JAMA)
items.summary: In a 14-centre Chinese randomised trial of 499 patients with AV block, LVEF of 50% or more and expected ventricular pacing above 40%, left bundle-branch area pacing (LBBAP) lowered the 24-month risk of death, heart failure events or biventricular upgrade vs right ventricular pacing (Kaplan-Meier 5.0% vs 13.2%; HR 0.37) (JAMA, Oct 28, 2026).
bullets: **LEAP-Block** (JAMA, 28 Oct 2026): **left bundle-branch area pacing (LBBAP) vs right ventricular pacing (RVP)** in **AV block with LVEF ≥50%**.
**14 Chinese hospitals**; **499 randomised** (249 vs 250), **482 analysed**; mean age **67**, **46% female**; anticipated pacing burden **>40%**.
**Primary endpoint** (death, HF event or upgrade to BiV pacing) at 24 months: Kaplan-Meier **5.0% with LBBAP vs 13.2% with RVP**, **HR 0.37** (95% CI 0.19-0.73; **P=0.004**).
**HF events** (secondary): **3.4% vs 11.3%**. Death, BiV upgrade, device complications and pacing-induced cardiomyopathy did not differ significantly on their own.
**Procedural success** was similar (**97.9% vs 99.6%**); **LBB capture** was confirmed in **79.7%**.
Benefit was **consistent across prespecified subgroups**; **superiority** design with 24-month follow-up in a Chinese population.

Limits: single country; blinding not stated in the abstract. Its crude composite (2.4% vs 12.5%) is below its own HF-event rate (3.4%) and its dates conflict, so only the Kaplan-Meier estimate is used.
